 Kelsey says Cards 'stunk' as Tigers roar out of 18-point hole, win in rout 
 By RUSS BROWN, Kentucky Today
 Russ Brown 
 Author email

 Nov 15, 2026

 If you had watched as Louisville led by as many as 18 points in the first half of its game with Memphis, then had taken a break and tuned back in late in the second half, you would have been in for a shock. Sort of like the Cardinals were.
 Host Memphis (3-1) stormed back from that early deficit to dominate the second half in every area and engineered a remarkable 38-point turnaround to stun No. 10 U of L, 98-78, in the FedEx Forum.
 It goes down as the fourth biggest comeback by an unranked team against a top 10 club in 15 years.
 The comeback produced some astounding numbers that Card Nation probably thought they'd never see out of such an experienced group featuring eight transfers, starting with the 57-26 blowout in the final 20 minutes.
 Louisville forward Alvaro Folgueiras, left, defends Memphis guard Jayden Reid (0) during the first half of an NCAA basketball game Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in Memphis, Tenn. (AP Photo/Nikki Boertman)
 Nikki Boertman 
 The Tigers, who trailed 52-41 at intermission immediately turned the tables on Louisville, which had hit 13 of its first 16 shots to start the game. The winners began the second half with a 12-3 run and were just getting warmed up. They hit 13 of their first 15 field goal attempts. They took their first lead, 62-59, with six minutes into the period and continued to build it. 
 The Cards (2-1) couldn't throw the ball in the Mississippi, going over nine minutes without a field goal while falling behind 91-72 and missing 17 consecutive 3-pointers during a stretch of futility that began late in the first half. After making 7-of-14 shots from distance in the first half, they missed all 15 attempts behind the arc the rest of the way, while plummeting from 56.5% overall in the first 20 minutes to 32.5%.
 Memphis hit 20-of-27 shots in the second half, including 7-of-10 trifectas, to finish 34-of-59 overall for 57.7%. The Tigers hit open threes and blew by stationary Cards for layups. They also had nine steals and seven blocks for the game.
 "I've never been involved in anything like this," U of L coach Pat Kelsey said on his postgame radio show. "We were absolutely annihilated. It was a butt-freaking whupping in every form and fashion. That's unacceptable. You've got to give Memphis credit because they were the aggressor and they were terrific. But we let them be terrific.
 Louisville head coach Pat Kelsey instructs his team during the second half of an NCAA college basketball game against Memphis, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in Memphis, Tenn. (AP Photo/Nikki Boertman)
 Nikki Boertman 
 "It got away from us in the second half. It snowballed and we unraveled. We stunk out loud for the last 32 minutes. How they respond to what's going to come their way is going to be important because the criticism is coming and it is warranted. I hope they turn off their phones and don't listen to it. I know one thing; we are going to get after it and fix it."
 Point guard Jayden Reid, who Kelsey said he tried to recruit at the College of Charleston, was unstoppable for the Tigers. He got 24 points, 10 assists, five rebounds and four steals. Tylik Weeks also had 24 points, along with five rebounds and four steals, while Julius Thedford contributed 16 points and Rikards Vavers added 15.
 For U of L, Seth Trimble and Jackson Shelstad each scored 16 points and Alvaro Folgueras had 14.
 The Cards will host Stetson Thursday night.
